title: console: a route whose object read was answered (5xx, or a 404 with an unknown code) says "check your connection" instead of the server's reason
body:
domain:ui#5 · zhuangjianguo · session_01QsR2jQjvWkZ7is6GXbC6DB

Filing gate: ② out-of-scope finding, class b (read, not yet measured), from #29704. The seat kept it out of that card's claim because the fix runs through `appObjectScope.ts`, the landing site of seat 2's #29681 and #29552 (claim amendment on #29704). Filed by `domain:ui#5`. ⛔ Not a claim. No grade: triage sets it.

**Business reason.** When an app route cannot load its object, the page asks the person to check their network, even though the server answered with a clear reason. That is the same defect #29704 fixes on the list, record and related-list states. The route-level state is the one left.

## What happens (by reading at `7b55ea95`; measure first)

- `MetadataProvider` marks a by-name object read `failed` on an answered 5xx, or on a 404 whose code it does not know. The read happened; it was answered.
- `AppContent`'s `RouteObjectReadFailed` (~L2112) then draws the generic sentence "check your connection and try again". The route keeps only the failed names, not the error, so it cannot show the server's code or sentence.

## Wanted

The same rule #29704 introduces, through the shared helper it adds to `@object-ui/react` (`utils/error-message.ts`). An answered failure shows the server's code and sentence, and the network sentence is only for a request that got no answer. To do that, the by-name read state keeps the error, or at least its status, code and message, beside the failed name.

## Tests

Over the real `MetadataProvider` and route, with a recording adapter:
- an answered 503 shows its code and sentence;
- a request that got no answer shows the network sentence;
- an ablation reds the first.

Serialize after #29704's PR, which adds the helper, and after #29681 and #29552's leg on `appObjectScope.ts`.

Landing site: `ui/packages/app-shell/src/providers/MetadataProvider.tsx`, `console/appObjectScope.ts`, `console/AppContent.tsx`.

Dedupe: `is:issue RouteObjectReadFailed`, `is:issue check your connection answered` (none open).

Links back: #29704, #29673.
